content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in the horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low or negative (sentiment < 0.05) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lag in price increases: model often delays upward moves by 1–3 days relative to true price acceleration.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to recent volatility, especially after sharp spikes — true price tends to revert to prior 10–15 day average.
- Overshoot after sentiment-driven spikes: if sentiment > 0.15 and price rises sharply, model forecasts 5–10% above true outcome.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days of forecast) — adjust downward by 2–5% for final 10 days.
- Sentiment correlation: if sentiment > 0.10, model should add 0.5–1.5% to forecast; if sentiment < 0.05, subtract 0.5–1.5% — sentiment amplifies or dampens forecast bias.
